EXPERIENCE.headline: Beautiful photographs begin with feeling comfortable enough to be yourself.
EXPERIENCE.lead: Being in front of a camera doesn’t come naturally to everyone. That’s where I come in.
body: I’ll guide you through the process, find the beautiful light, help with the little details, and give you direction when you need it. You don’t have to know what to do with your hands or how to pose. That’s my job.
Along the way, we’ll laugh, move around, try things, and leave room for the moments nobody could have planned.
My approach blends thoughtful direction with genuine connection, creating photographs that feel polished and beautiful without losing what makes them yours.
EXPERIENCE.closing: The goal isn’t simply to look incredible in your photographs. It’s to feel comfortable, confident, and genuinely enjoy creating them.

ABOUT.headline: Meet Shelly — the heart behind Firefly Photography.
ABOUT.lead: I believe the most memorable photographs come from genuine connection.
body: My approach combines an artistic eye with an easygoing, personable experience. I love finding beautiful light, noticing the small details, and creating images that feel both thoughtfully composed and naturally you.

Whether I’m photographing a wedding, a growing family, a graduating senior, or someone stepping in front of the camera for the first time, I want the experience to feel comfortable, enjoyable, and personal.
I’ll provide guidance, help you feel at ease, and encourage those moments of real laughter and connection that often become the photographs people treasure most.

It’s about remembering how it felt.

JOURNAL.title: What to Expect During Your Firefly Photography Session
JOURNAL.excerpt: Never been in front of a professional camera? Here’s exactly how a session with me works — from the first hello to your final gallery.
JOURNAL.seoTitle: What to Expect at Your Photo Session | Firefly Photography, Denver
JOURNAL.seoDescription: How a Firefly Photography portrait session works, step by step: planning, gentle posing direction, your proof gallery and choosing 15 favorites for detailed editing.

cover.alt: Couple laughing together in tall Colorado grass

JOURNAL.body:
Most people I photograph tell me the same thing before we start: “I’m so awkward in front of the camera.” If that’s you, you’re in good company — and you’re exactly who I love working with.

Here’s what a portrait session with me actually looks like, so you can walk in knowing what to expect.

Before the session: planning together

It starts with a conversation. You tell me what you’re envisioning — who’s in the photos, the feeling you want, any must-have shots — and we choose a location and time of day that gives us beautiful light. I’ll recommend Colorado spots that fit your style and share preparation and outfit guidance so nothing feels like guesswork.

During the session: you don’t have to know how to pose

This is the part people worry about most, and it’s the part I enjoy most. I’ll guide you the whole way: where to stand, what to do with your hands, how to angle toward the light, when to move. Between the composed portraits we’ll laugh, walk, try things and leave room for the moments nobody could have planned.

You don’t have to know what to do with your hands or how to pose. That’s my job.

After the session: your proof gallery

I review everything we captured and prepare a private online proof gallery of all the usable images. You’ll get to see the whole session, not just a handful of selects.

Choosing your 15 favorites

For standard portrait packages, you choose the 15 photographs you love most just by tapping the heart in your gallery. Those 15 go through my detailed editing process. You also receive the remaining usable proof images — so you end up with a broad collection of memories and a carefully refined collection of favorite portraits.

Weddings and elopements follow their own process and delivery, which we’ll go over together when you book.

The part that matters most

The goal isn’t simply to look incredible in your photographs. It’s to feel comfortable, confident, and genuinely enjoy creating them. If you’re ready, tell me your story — I’d love to hear it.

JOURNAL.title: Why Golden Hour Is So Beautiful for Outdoor Portraits
JOURNAL.excerpt: That warm, glowing light right before sunset isn’t just pretty — it’s the most flattering light of the day. Here’s why I plan sessions around it.
JOURNAL.seoTitle: Why Golden Hour Is Best for Outdoor Portraits | Denver Photographer
JOURNAL.seoDescription: What golden hour is, why it’s so flattering for portraits, and how Firefly Photography plans Denver and Colorado sessions around the best light.

cover.alt: Couple embracing in a meadow as the sun sets behind the mountains

JOURNAL.body:
If you’ve ever noticed how everyone looks a little more beautiful in the last hour before sunset, you’ve already discovered golden hour.

What is golden hour?

Golden hour is the time shortly after sunrise and before sunset when the sun sits low in the sky. Its light travels through more of the atmosphere, which softens it and warms it into those honey and amber tones we all love.

Why it’s so flattering

  • Soft light, soft shadows. Midday sun creates harsh shadows under eyes and noses. Low sun wraps gently around faces instead.
  • Warm, glowing skin. The warm color is naturally flattering on every skin tone.
  • Backlight and glow. With the sun behind you, I can create that dreamy rim of light in your hair and through tall grass.
  • No squinting. Lower, gentler light means relaxed eyes and natural expressions.

Golden hour in Colorado

Our mountains change the math a little. On the west side of Denver and in the foothills, the sun can drop behind the peaks earlier than the official sunset, so I plan start times around each location — not just the clock. Out on the open plains, we often get light a little longer.

What if golden hour doesn’t work for us?

Schedules are real, and little ones have bedtimes. Open shade, overcast days and soft window light at home can all be beautiful too — finding the best light wherever we are is part of my job.

Thinking about an outdoor session? Let’s find your light.

JOURNAL.title: How to Prepare for Your Newborn Photography Session
JOURNAL.excerpt: Simple, stress-free tips for an in-home newborn session — what to wear, how to get your home ready, and why there’s no such thing as a “perfect” baby day.
JOURNAL.seoTitle: Preparing for a Newborn Photo Session | Firefly Photography
JOURNAL.seoDescription: Practical tips for an in-home newborn photography session in Denver: timing, what to wear, preparing your space and keeping baby comfortable.

cover.alt: Parents smiling down at their newborn baby

JOURNAL.body:
The best newborn photos aren’t about elaborate props or perfect poses. They’re about the way you look at your baby — and that’s already there. Here’s how to make the session easy.

Relax: the session follows your baby

Newborn sessions are unhurried. Feeding breaks, diaper changes and cuddles are all part of the plan, and some of the sweetest images happen in between.

Getting your home ready

  • Light is everything. Open the curtains in the room with the most natural light — often a bedroom or living room. I’ll help find the best spot when I arrive.
  • Keep it warm. Newborns love a cozy room, especially if we capture some skin-to-skin moments.
  • Tidy one or two spaces. You don’t need a spotless house — just clear the area where we’ll photograph.

What to wear

Soft, neutral, comfortable clothes photograph beautifully and keep the attention on your baby. Think creams, soft whites, muted earth tones and simple textures. Avoid big logos and busy patterns. Barefoot is perfect.

Siblings and pets

Absolutely include them! I keep sibling photos short and playful, and a gentle family dog can make for some of the most treasured frames.

Most importantly

There’s no such thing as a “perfect” baby day — and you don’t need one. Bring your love; I’ll take care of the rest. See newborn sessions or tell me about your little one.

JOURNAL.title: 10 Beautiful Places for Family Photos Near Denver
JOURNAL.excerpt: From foothill meadows to tree-lined city parks, these are some of my favorite Denver-area spots for family photos — and what makes each one special.
JOURNAL.seoTitle: 10 Best Places for Family Photos Near Denver | Firefly Photography
JOURNAL.seoDescription: A Denver family photographer’s guide to beautiful family photo locations near Denver, Littleton, Morrison, Evergreen and Boulder — with tips on light and timing.

cover.alt: Family portrait on a Colorado hillside

JOURNAL.body:
One of the best parts of photographing families around Denver is how much variety is close by — open meadows, foothills, lakes and leafy city parks, often within a short drive.

Here are ten places I love, with a few notes on what makes each one special. (Some parks charge entry fees or require photography permits; we’ll talk it through when we plan your session.)

1. Chautauqua Park, Boulder

The Flatirons make an iconic backdrop, and the open meadow glows at golden hour.

2. Mount Falcon Park, Morrison

Sweeping foothill views and golden grasses — a favorite of mine for engagement and family sessions alike.

3. Red Rocks Park, Morrison

Dramatic red sandstone formations for families who want something bold and unmistakably Colorado.

4. Evergreen Lake, Evergreen

Water, pines and mountain light. Gorgeous in fall, and magical with a dusting of snow.

5. Lair o’ the Bear Park, Idledale

A creek, cottonwoods and wooded trails — perfect for playful, wandering sessions with kids.

6. Chatfield State Park, Littleton

Open prairie, water views and long, soft evening light on the plains side of the metro area.

7. Washington Park, Denver

Classic tree-lined paths, gardens and lakes right in the city — easy for families with little ones.

8. Hudson Gardens, Littleton

Lush, beautifully kept gardens for a romantic, timeless feel.

9. Deer Creek Canyon, Littleton

Rolling foothills and wide open sky just minutes from town.

10. Your own backyard

Honestly? Some of my favorite family sessions happen at home, where everyone is most relaxed.

Choosing the right spot for your family

Think about the feeling you want: wide open and airy, or cozy and wooded? How far are your kids willing to walk? And what time of day can you realistically be there? I’ll help match a location to your family and plan around the best light. See family sessions or start planning yours.
